assumptions.a_values: Component values from the kicadsexpr netlist export of hardware/pcb/qssc.kicad_sch (126 components, 172 nets; parsed 2026-09-19): C31=220p NP0, C32=10n, C33=220p NP0, R67=1k, R68=2.2k, C34=100p, C35=100p, L2=100n.
assumptions.b_cap_ideal: Capacitors modelled ideal (no ESR/ESL). C31/C33 are NP0 per netlist notes; C32 X7R dielectric tolerance affects absolute BW, not the cross-engine comparison.
assumptions.c_cp_ideal: Charge pump modelled as ideal current source (pulse/step); ADF4351 CP output impedance and switching transients not modelled.
assumptions.e_kvco: Kvco = 40 MHz/V (ADF4351 datasheet-typical). Real Kvco varies with tuning voltage; this scales the derived loop bandwidth linearly.
assumptions.g_esd_cap: D3 ESD5V0 modelled as pure junction capacitance; the schematic carries no capacitance value, so 0.3 pF (low-cap ESD variant) and 1 pF (generic 5 V ESD) are both simulated.
assumptions.h_rail_ac_gnd: +5V_RF treated as AC ground (7x 100nF decoupling + FB1 600 ohm); L2 therefore modelled as a shunt inductor to ground in the RF decks.
assumptions.i_amp_model: GVA-84+ modelled as a unilateral ideal amplifier: G=16 dB, Zin=Zout=50 ohm, S12=0 (section 6: 16 dB @ 3 GHz). NF and OIP3 not simulated.
assumptions.j_engines: ngspice-47 as the independent engine; identical element values, no shared physics code path. Both SP models are behavioural idealisations, so SP cross-engine agreement validates the harness, not the amp model choice.
assumptions.k_bleed: The ladder CP node carries a 10 Mohm shunt to ground in both engines (CP output impedance / leakage proxy). SPICE requires a DC path at every node for the operating point; qucsator AC does not, but the same shunt is added there to keep the netlists identical. It is negligible at all probe frequencies (Xc31(1 kHz) = 723k).
assumptions.l_ipulse_t2: qucsator Ipulse T2 is the ABSOLUTE pulse stop time, not the width (width = T2 - T1). Verified in the pilot run via the plateau charge: T1=10n/T2=20n produced a 1.88 mV plateau (~21.9 pC into 10.44 nF total ladder capacitance = 10 ns of 2.19 mA), while the ngspice PULSE(20n) produced 4.32 mV (~43.8 pC = 20 ns). The qucsator pulse deck therefore uses T2=30n so both engines drive the same 43.8 pC.
assumptions.m_amp_g_linear: The qucsator Amp device parameter G is a LINEAR voltage gain, not dB. Empirically verified in the pilot run: G=16 produced |S21| = 24.01 dB ~= 20*log10(16). 16 dB is therefore set as G = 10^(16/20) = 6.3096.

checks.claim: CP pulse response (20 ns, Icp) final decay agrees across engines; peak value agrees within 10 mV.

checks.void_reason: VOID after the pilot run. The 7.008 V DC expectation has no valid DC path in this deck: C33 blocks the ladder from LF_OUT, so the only DC path is the 10 Mohm bleed (assumption k), which puts the DC asymptote at Icp*10 Mohm = 21.9 kV with a bleed time constant far beyond the 2 ms window. The ~400 V tails seen in both engines are the unconverged bleed ramp, not ladder physics. The check as pre-registered is a bad check (garbage-in) and is voided rather than redesigned mid-run (eco F3 lesson: check the deck before redesigning). The real board's DC path is the ADF4351 CP output / VCO tuning-port input impedance, which is intentionally not modelled here.
